IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r10.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r10.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r10.claim: واقترب in 21:96–97 is another cited instance of an extra coordinating waw.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r10.anchor: وكقوله: حتى إذا فتحت يأجوج ومأجوج وهم من كل حدب ينسلون (96) واقترب الوعد الحق [الأنبياء: 96، 97] .

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p92/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p92/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p92/r3.claim: The conclusion reassures the Prophet and companions that all prophets taught one message; they should persist and leave those who divided it to God, since late faith will not help.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p92/r3.anchor: all prophets of God have taught the same message they are preaching

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p92/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p92/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p92/r4.claim: Only God's pious servants attain the Hereafter's success; judgement is near, and the Prophet ends by supplicating God to judge between him and his foes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p92/r4.anchor: a decisive declaration is made from the tongue of the Prophet (sws) that the time of judgement is at hand

TABATABAI:18:98-102/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:98-102/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:98-102/r1.claim: The preceding account of Gog and Magog breaking loose and the true promise approaching is an eschatological portent.
TABATABAI:18:98-102/r1.anchor: الأنبياء 96-97. وهي على أي حال من الملاحم

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p149/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p149/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p149/r6.claim: The sūrah’s closing section resumes its opening warning about the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p149/r6.anchor: Warning people of the Hereafter with which the sūrah began is taken up again here.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p149/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p149/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p149/r7.claim: This return to the opening guides readers to the Qur’an’s coherence, a style found in most sūrahs; it restores the sūrah’s real purpose if its expanse obscures it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p149/r7.anchor: The benefit of this style is that if the real purpose of a sūrah is lost in its expanse, it is brought before the addressees once again.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p152/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p152/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p152/r3.claim: People consider the Judgment far away, but it is near by God's measure; humans judge time by their short standards, unlike God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p152/r3.anchor: they regard it to be far off, and We see it very near at hand

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p152/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p152/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p152/r4.claim: The Judgment's sudden arrival will horrify those who demanded it and mocked it, leaving them staring in fear and consternation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p152/r4.anchor: will be struck with fear and consternation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p152/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p152/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p152/r5.claim: The confession begins with an omitted speech verb; disbelievers admit that messengers tried to awaken them, yet they wronged themselves and mocked the warnings.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p152/r5.anchor: God did send people for this purpose who did their utmost to awaken them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p152/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p152/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p152/r6.claim: The obstacle to belief is indifference, not a lack of evidence: the Judgment conflicts with people's desires, so they defer preparation until it arrives.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p152/r6.anchor: the real impediment is the indifference of people.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p467/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p467/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p467/r10.claim: The true promise is the certain promise of resurrection; the verb iqtaraba conveys greater nearness than qaruba.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p467/r10.anchor: واقترب الوعد الحق أي الوعد بالبعث الحق الذي لا شك فيه واقترب قيل: أبلغ في القرب من قرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p467/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p467/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p467/r11.claim: The pronoun hiya can be a pronoun of the event, with shākhisa as predicate and abṣāru as subject; raising abṣāru as a sentence after a pronoun of شأن or qiṣṣa is barred by the stated Basran analysis but allowed by Kufans.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p467/r11.anchor: وضمير هي للقصة كأنه قيل: فإذا القصة والحادثة أبصار الذين كفروا شاخصة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p467/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p467/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p467/r12.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats hiya as a vague pronoun clarified by abṣāru, as in the construction ‘those who did wrong kept quiet.’
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p467/r12.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: هي ضمير مبهم توضحه الأبصار وتفسره كما فسر الذين ظلموا وأسروا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p467/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p467/r13.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p467/r13.claim: Al-Farraʾ says hiya is a pronoun for the eyes, advanced because the following words explain it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p467/r13.anchor: قال الفراء: هي ضمير الأبصار تقدمت لدلالة الكلام ومجيء ما يفسرها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r1.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r1.claim: Al-Farraʾ also takes hiya as a separator pronoun that can be replaced by huwa; the author says this only works under al-Kisāʾī’s view that the separator may precede the predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r1.anchor: وذكر أيضا الفراء أن هي عماد يصلح في موضعها هو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r2.speaker: الثعلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r2.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi ends the clause at fa-idha hiya (‘then it appears/occurs’), then starts ‘the eyes of the unbelievers are staring’; the author calls this forced and discordant syntax.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r2.anchor: وذكر الثعلبي وجها آخر وهو أن الكلام ثم عند قوله: فإذا هي أي بارزة واقعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r3.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r3.claim: Al-Farraʾ cites a poetic line beginning ‘By her father, my beloved says nothing except …’ as evidence for advancing a pronoun whose antecedent is clarified later.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r3.anchor: فلا وأبيها لا تقول خليلتي ... إلا قر عني مالك بن أبي كعب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r4.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r4.claim: Al-Farraʾ cites a second poem for hiya as a separator replaceable by huwa; the author says the analysis relies on a disputed placement of the separator before its predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r4.anchor: بثوب ودينار وشاة ودرهم ... فهل هو مرفوع بما هاهنا رأس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari supplies ‘they say’ for yā waylanā and treats the saying as a circumstantial clause describing the unbelievers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r6.anchor: يا ويلنا معمول لقول محذوف. قال الزمخشري: تقديره يقولون وهو في موضع الحال من الذين كفروا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r7.claim: Shukhūṣ is fixing one’s gaze without blinking; ‘we were heedless of this’ refers to the truths they have now found and recognized.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r7.anchor: والشخوص إحداد النظر دون أن يطرف في غفلة من هذا انتهى. أي مما وجدنا الآن وتبينا من الحقائق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r8.claim: Their ‘rather, we were wrongdoers’ retracts the claim of inadvertent heedlessness and admits their deliberate unbelief and turning away from faith.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p468/r8.anchor: ثم أضربوا عن قولهم قد كنا في غفلة وأخبروا بما قد كانوا تعمدوه من الكفر والإعراض عن الإيمان

RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r11.claim: The true promise that has approached is unquestionably the Day of Resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r11.anchor: لا شبهة أن الوعد المذكور هو يوم القيامة

RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r12.claim: Here إذا marks suddenness; وعد is a figurative name for the appointed event, and إذا can stand in the result for the fā, as in 30:36.
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r12.anchor: فاعلم أن إذا ههنا للمفاجأة فسمى الموعد وعدا تجوزا

RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r13.claim: The fā can accompany إذا and reinforce the connection between condition and result; either فإذا هي شاخصة or فهي شاخصة is sound.
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r13.anchor: فإذا جاءت الفاء معها تعاونتا على وصل الجزاء بالشرط

RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r14.claim: One grammatical analysis makes هي refer to the eyes, first referring to them implicitly and then naming them explicitly.
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r14.anchor: أحدها : أن تكون كناية عن الأبصار ، والمعنى فإذا أبصار الذين كفروا شاخصة

RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r15.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r15.claim: Al-Farrāʾ treats هي as an ʿimād pronoun, replaceable by masculine هو; feminine agreement suits الأبصار, while masculine suits the ʿimād construction.
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r15.anchor: وجاز التأنيث لأن الأبصار مؤنثة وجاز التذكير للعماد وهو قول الفراء

RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r16.speaker: سيبويه
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r16.claim: Sībawayh takes هي to refer to the story or event: the event is that the unbelievers’ eyes stare fixedly then.
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r16.anchor: وقال سيبويه الضمير للقصة بمعنى فإذا القصة شاخصة

RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r17.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r17.claim: At the Resurrection the unbelievers’ eyes stare without nearly blinking, from the day’s horrors and fear of what awaits them.
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r17.anchor: أن القيامة إذا قامت شخصت أبصار هؤلاء من شدة الأهوال

RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r18.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r18.claim: An omitted يقولون is understood before يا ويلنا: they say, “Woe to us.”
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r18.anchor: واعلم أنه لا بد قبل قوله يا ويلنا من حذف والتقدير يقولون يا ويلنا

RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r19.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r19.claim: They admit that in worldly life they were heedless of this, denying that it would happen.
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r19.anchor: يعني في الدنيا حيث كذبناه وقلنا

RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r20.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r20.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r20.claim: They confess that their heedlessness and denial of Muhammad, along with worship of idols, wronged themselves.
RAZI-FULL:v22p192/r20.anchor: بل كنا ظالمين أنفسنا بتلك الغفلة وبتكذيب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وعبادة الأوثان

STUDYQURAN:21:97/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:97/r1.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:21:97/r1.claim: The emergence of Gog and Magog signals that the end of the world is approaching.
STUDYQURAN:21:97/r1.anchor: The coming of Gog and Magog is a sign of the impending end of the world (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:21:97/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:97/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:21:97/r2.claim: “The true promise” refers to the Day of Resurrection.
STUDYQURAN:21:97/r2.anchor: The true promise refers to the Day of Resurrection (R)

STUDYQURAN:21:97/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:97/r3.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:21:97/r3.claim: The second phrase may alternatively be read, “The stare of those who disbelieved will be fixed.”
STUDYQURAN:21:97/r3.anchor: The second phrase of this verse could also be read to mean, “The stare of those who disbelieved will be fixed” (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:21:97/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:97/r4.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:21:97/r4.claim: Their fixed stare results from fear in the face of the terrifying event.
STUDYQURAN:21:97/r4.anchor: which will occur because of the fear they experience in the face of this horrible event (Q, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:21:97/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:97/r5.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:21:97/r5.claim: The disbelievers’ confession of heedlessness reflects their inattention to these matters during worldly life.
STUDYQURAN:21:97/r5.anchor: We have certainly been heedless of this reflects the fact that in the life of the world they paid no attention to such matters (R)

STUDYQURAN:21:97/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:97/r6.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:21:97/r6.claim: Symbolically, Gog and Magog are the preoccupations, tumult, and impressions that assault and corrupt the soul and expose it to satanic influence.
STUDYQURAN:21:97/r6.anchor: Gog and Magog represent, at the level of spiritual symbolism, the preoccupations, tumult, and impressions that assault the soul

TAB-FULL:v16p408#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p408#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p408#2/r1.claim: After Gog and Magog are released, God's true promise of resurrection from the graves for reward and punishment draws near.
TAB-FULL:v16p408#2/r1.anchor: والعقاب، وهو لا شك حق، كما قال جل ثناؤه

TAB-FULL:v16p408#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p408#2/r2.speaker: حذيفة
TAB-FULL:v16p408#2/r2.claim: Ḥudhayfa says that after Gog and Magog emerge, even a foal raised by a man would not be ridden before the Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v16p408#2/r2.anchor: ثنا حذيفة: «لو أن رجلا، افتلى فلوا بعد خروج يأجوج ومأجوج

TAB-FULL:v16p408#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p408#2/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p408#2/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses the true promise drawing near as the Day of Resurrection approaching them.
TAB-FULL:v16p408#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {واقترب الوعد الحق}

TAB-FULL:v16p408#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p408#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p408#2/r4.claim: Ṭabarī treats the conjunction wāw as inserted; the intended sequence is that once Gog and Magog are released, the true promise draws near.

TAB-FULL:v16p408#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p408#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p408#2/r5.claim: He compares the conjunction to 37:104, understood without its wāw, and cites an Imruʾ al-Qays line with successive unjoined verbs.
TAB-FULL:v16p408#2/r5.anchor: وذلك نظير قوله: {فلما أسلما وتله للجبين وناديناه}

TAB-FULL:v16p408#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p408#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p408#2/r6.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays's poetic line uses an unjoined successive verb to illustrate the conjunction analysis.
TAB-FULL:v16p408#2/r6.anchor: فلما أجزنا ساحة الحي وانتحى … بنا بطن خبت ذي حقاف عقنقل

TAB-FULL:v16p410/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p410/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p410/r1.claim: One analysis makes هي refer to the eyes, with أبصار الذين كفروا clarifying it; an anonymous poem offers a similar pronoun followed by its referent.
TAB-FULL:v16p410/r1.anchor: أحدهما أن تكون كناية عن الأبصار

TAB-FULL:v16p410/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p410/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p410/r2.claim: Alternatively, هي is a supporting pronoun (ʿimād), as in 22:46; Ṭabarī also adduces a poetic parallel.
TAB-FULL:v16p410/r2.anchor: والثاني: أن تكون عمادا، كما قال جل ثناؤه: {فإنها لا تعمى الأبصار}

TAB-FULL:v16p410#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p410#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p410#2/r1.claim: The disbelievers' lament is understood as their response to the horrors of the Hour: they now see and endure what they had ignored.
TAB-FULL:v16p410#2/r1.anchor: وذلك (يقولون) من قوله: {فإذا هي شاخصة أبصار الذين كفروا}

TAB-FULL:v16p410#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p410#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p410#2/r2.claim: The text leaves out “they say,” which is understood from the preceding description of the disbelievers' staring eyes.
TAB-FULL:v16p410#2/r2.anchor: وفي الكلام متروك ترك ذكره استغناء بدلالة ما ذكر عليه عنه، وذلك (يقولون) من قوله

TABATABAI:2:21-25#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:21-25#7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:21-25#7/r1.claim: Among predictions of later events are the opening of Gog and Magog, the believers' succession in the land, and punishments descending on people from above or below.
TABATABAI:2:21-25#7/r1.anchor: وحرام على قرية أهلكناها أنهم لا يرجعون حتى إذا فتحت يأجوج ومأجوج وهم من كل حدب ينسلون

TABATABAI:21:96-97/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:96-97/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:96-97/r3.claim: He rejects that reading: the preceding opening, approaching promise, circumstantial syntax, and emergence from every height do not fit people leaving graves.
TABATABAI:21:96-97/r3.anchor: لا يصدق على الخروج من القبور

TABATABAI:21:97-101/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:97-101/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:97-101/r1.claim: The true promise that has drawn near is the Hour.

TABATABAI:21:97-101/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:97-101/r2.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:21:97-101/r2.claim: Raghib defines fixed gaze as looking without eyelids blinking; it signals intense attention without distraction and often sudden evil.
TABATABAI:21:97-101/r2.anchor: شخوص البصر نظره بحيث لا تطرف أجفانه، كذا ذكره الراغب وهو لازم كمال اهتمام الناظر

TABATABAI:21:97-101/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:97-101/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:97-101/r3.claim: When the Hour suddenly appears, the disbelievers call woe upon themselves and claim they had been made heedless of what they now see.
TABATABAI:21:97-101/r3.anchor: حكاية قول الكفار إذا شاهدوا الساعة بغتة فدعوا لأنفسهم بالويل مدعين أنهم غفلوا عما يشاهدونه

TABATABAI:21:97-101/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:97-101/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:97-101/r4.claim: They correct their excuse by admitting that their heedlessness came from injustice: worldly preoccupations made them forget the afterlife.
TABATABAI:21:97-101/r4.anchor: أضربوا عن ذلك بالإعتراف بأن الغفلة لم تنشأ إلا عن ظلمهم بالاشتغال بما ينسي الآخرة

TABRISI:21:97/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:97/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:21:97/r18.claim: شخص denotes traveling away from one’s home or city; a fixed gaze is described as though the eye had gone out toward its object.
TABRISI:21:97/r18.anchor: وشخص المسافر شخوصا إذا خرج من منزله وشخص من بلد إلى بلد وشخص بصره إذا نظر إليه

TABRISI:21:97/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:97/r20.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:21:97/r20.claim: Al-Farra says the wāw is extra: the meaning is that when Yajuj and Majuj are opened, the true promise draws near.
TABRISI:21:97/r20.anchor: قال الفراء: معنى الواو الطرح والمعنى إذا فتحت يأجوج ومأجوج اقترب الوعد الحق

TABRISI:21:97/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:97/r21.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:21:97/r21.claim: Al-Zajjaj says Basran grammarians do not allow dropping the wāw; the answer to إذا is يا ويلنا, with “they said” understood.
TABRISI:21:97/r21.anchor: قال الزجاج: الواو لا يجوز أن يطرح عند البصريين وجواب إذا عندهم قوله { يا ويلنا }

TABRISI:21:97/r22.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:97/r22.speaker: author
TABRISI:21:97/r22.claim: One parse makes إذا a locative adverb governed by شاخصة, هي a pronoun of the situation, and أبصار a second subject with fronted predicate; the sentence predicates of هي.
TABRISI:21:97/r22.anchor: إذا ظرف مكان والعامل فيه شاخصة وهي ضمير القصة في محل رفع بالابتداء وأبصار الذين كفروا مبتدأ آخر

TABRISI:21:97/r23.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:97/r23.speaker: author
TABRISI:21:97/r23.claim: Alternatively, the clause ends after هي, meaning that the event is present and near; a new sentence then says the disbelievers’ eyes are fixed, with the predicate fronted.
TABRISI:21:97/r23.anchor: وقيل: إن تمام الكلام عند قوله هي وتقديره فإذا هي بارزة واقعة

TABRISI:21:97/r24.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:97/r24.speaker: قتادة وابن مسعود والجبائي وأبو مسلم
TABRISI:21:97/r24.claim: Yajuj and Majuj descend rapidly from every elevation and spread throughout the land, leaving no hill without people rushing down it.
TABRISI:21:97/r24.anchor: من كل نشز من الأرض يسرعون عن قتادة وابن مسعود والجبائي وأبي مسلم يعني أنهم يتفرقون في الأرض

TABRISI:21:97-102/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:97-102/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:21:97-102/r3.claim: The true promise is the promised event, namely the approach of the Resurrection.
TABRISI:21:97-102/r3.anchor: أي الموعود الصدق ومعناه اقترب قيام الساعة

TABRISI:21:97-102/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:97-102/r4.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:21:97-102/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi says the disbelievers’ eyes will stare without nearly blinking, as they watch the terrors of that day.
TABRISI:21:97-102/r4.anchor: تشخص في ذلك اليوم أي لا تكاد تطرف من شدة ذلك اليوم وهوله ينظرون إلى تلك الأهوال عن الكلبي.

TABRISI:21:97-102/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:97-102/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:21:97-102/r5.claim: The phrase introduces what the disbelievers will say: “Woe to us!”
TABRISI:21:97-102/r5.anchor: { يا ويلنا } أي يقولون يا ويلنا

TABRISI:21:97-102/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:97-102/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:21:97-102/r6.claim: They confess that worldly affairs occupied them and they failed to reflect on the Resurrection.
TABRISI:21:97-102/r6.anchor: اشتغلنا بأمور الدنيا وغفلنا عن هذا اليوم فلم نتفكر فيه

TABRISI:21:97-102/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:97-102/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:21:97-102/r7.claim: They admit wrongdoing because they disobeyed God and worshipped another.
TABRISI:21:97-102/r7.anchor: بأن عصينا الله تعالى وعبدنا غيره

THALABI:v6p308/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p308/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p308/r4.claim: The true promise that has drawn near is the Resurrection.

THALABI:v6p308/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p308/r5.speaker: الفراء وجماعة من العلماء
THALABI:v6p308/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and other scholars treat the wāw as extra, construing the sentence as the true promise drawing near once Gog and Magog are released; they compare 37:103 and a poetic usage.
THALABI:v6p308/r5.anchor: قال الفراء وجماعة من العلماء: الواو في قوله «واقترب» مقحم ومجاز الآية:

THALABI:v6p308/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p308/r6.speaker: حذيفة
THALABI:v6p308/r6.claim: Ḥudhayfah says that someone acquiring a foal after Gog and Magog emerge would not ride it before the Hour.
THALABI:v6p308/r6.anchor: حديث حذيفة قال: لو أن رجلا اقتنى فلوا بعد خروج يأجوج ومأجوج لم يركبه

THALABI:v6p308/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p308/r7.speaker: الزجاج
THALABI:v6p308/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj and the Basrans reject omission of the wāw; they make the response to ḥattā idhā the disbelievers' cry, with the promise also drawing near.
THALABI:v6p308/r7.anchor: وقال الزجاج: البصريون لا يجيزون طرح الواو ويجعلون جواب حتى إذا

THALABI:v6p308/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p308/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p308/r8.claim: One parse makes hiyya a pronoun for the eyes, with the explicit word eyes explaining it.
THALABI:v6p308/r8.anchor: أحدها: أن تكون هي كناية عن الأبصار ويكون الأبصار الظاهرة بيانا عنها

THALABI:v6p308/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p308/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p308/r9.claim: A second parse treats hiyya as a supporting pronoun, with parallels from the Qur'an and poetry.
THALABI:v6p308/r9.anchor: والثاني: أن تكون هي عمادا كقوله «فإنها لا تعمى الأبصار»

THALABI:v6p308/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p308/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p308/r10.claim: A third parse ends the clause at hiyya, meaning that the event is manifest and near; then the eyes of the disbelievers, terrified at the Resurrection, are described as staring, with the predicate preceding its subject.
THALABI:v6p308/r10.anchor: والثالث: أن يكون تمام الكلام عند قوله هي على معنى هي بارزة واقفة

THALABI:v6p308/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p308/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p308/r11.claim: The disbelievers cry woe, admitting they had been heedless of this Day.
THALABI:v6p308/r11.anchor: وهم يقولون يا ويلنا قد كنا في غفلة من هذا أي من هذا اليوم

THALABI:v6p308/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p308/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p308/r12.claim: They acknowledge wrongdoing through disobeying God and assigning worship to the wrong place.
THALABI:v6p308/r12.anchor: بل كنا ظالمين بمعصيتنا ربنا ووضعنا العبادة في غير موضعها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p201/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p201/r1.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p201/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ treats the wāw as extra: the meaning is that when Gog and Magog are released, the true promise draws near; he compares 39:73 and 37:103–104.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p201/r1.anchor: - قوله تعالى: {واقترب} اختلفوا في هذه الواو: فقال الفراء: الواو مقحمة زائدة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p201/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p201/r2.speaker: الكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p201/r2.claim: Al-Kisāʾī agrees that Arabs may use a semantically dispensable wāw in the response to ḥattā idhā, lammā, ḥīna, and similar temporal clauses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p201/r2.anchor: ونحو هذا قال الكسائي (¬1) قال: والعرب تدخل الواو في جواب (حتى إذا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p201/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p201/r3.speaker: امرؤ القيس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p201/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ cites Imruʾ al-Qays’s line and takes intahā as the sense, with the preceding wāw contributing no meaning.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p201/r3.anchor: وأنشد قول امرىء القيس (¬1): فلما أجزنا ساحة الحي وانتحى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p201/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p201/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p201/r4.claim: Abū Isḥāq rejects a dispensable wāw in Basran grammar and supplies an omitted answer to ḥattā idhā: after Gog and Magog are released and the promise nears, they say “Woe to us.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p201/r4.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: والواو عند البصريين لا يجوز أن تدخل ويكون معناها الطرح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p201/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p201/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p201/r5.claim: The emergence of Gog and Magog is one of the signs of the Hour.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p201/r5.anchor: وخروج يأجوج ومأجوج من أعلام الساعة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the true promise as the Resurrection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r1.anchor: {الوعد الحق} قال ابن عباس: يريد القيامة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r2.speaker: الكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r2.claim: Al-Kisāʾī allows wa-qtarraba to coordinate with idhā futiḥat, making fa-idhā hiya shākhisah the answer to both clauses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r2.anchor: قال الكسائي (¬3): ويجوز أن يكون واقترب عطفا على "إذا فتحت"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says hiya can be a support pronoun equivalent to huwa; the feminine agrees with the feminine word eyes, while the support pronoun may be masculine, as at 27:9 and 22:46.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r4.claim: An Arab expression and a cited verse illustrate huwa as a support pronoun; the poem’s “fa-hal huwa marfūʿ” is another example.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r4.anchor: قال: وسمعت بعض العرب يقول: كان مرة وهو ينفع الناس أحسابهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r5.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r5.claim: Alternatively, hiya anticipates al-abṣār and the later phrase explains it, an ellipsis on the condition of interpretation, as in a cited line that names the referent afterward.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r5.anchor: وإن شئت جعلت "هي" للأبصار كنيت عنها، ثم أظهرت الأبصار لتفسيرها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r6.claim: The commentary points to its discussion of this explanatory ellipsis at 12:77.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r6.anchor: وقد ذكرنا معنى الإضمار على شريطة التفسير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r7.speaker: المبرد، سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r7.claim: Al-Mubarrad, citing Sibawayh, says a masculine report takes a masculine pronoun meaning “the matter,” while a feminine report may take a feminine pronoun meaning “the story.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r7.anchor: وقال المبرد -في هذه الآية-: قال سيبويه؛ إذا كان الخبر عن مذكر فحق الاضمار أن يكون بعلامة التذكير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r8.speaker: المبرد، سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r8.claim: The masculine construction is illustrated by 20:74 and 72:3; a feminine story-pronoun may be used for a feminine predicate, though a masculine affair-pronoun is also valid.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p203/r8.anchor: نحو قوله: {إنه من يأت ربه مجرما}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p206/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p206/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p206/r1.claim: He gives a third construal of the pronoun: the implied subject is ‘the matter/story,’ namely that the disbelievers’ eyes are fixed when the promise arrives.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p206/r1.anchor: وقد يكون التقدير في الآية: فإذا القصة شاخصة أبصار الذين كفروا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p206/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p206/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p206/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī says the disbelievers’ eyes stare without nearly blinking from the day’s terror and severity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p206/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي: شخصت أبصار الكفار فلا تكاد تطرف من شدة ذلك اليوم وهوله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p206/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p206/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p206/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains their confession of heedlessness as their worldly blindness to what was required of them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p206/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد في الدنيا كنا في عماية عما يراد منا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p206/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p206/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p206/r4.claim: Their admission that they were wrongdoers means they wronged themselves by denying Muḥammad and taking deities.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p206/r4.anchor: أنفسنا بتكذيب محمد -صلى الله عليه وسلم- واتخاذ الآلهة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:97-99/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:97-99/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:97-99/r1.claim: The true promise is the Resurrection.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:97-99/r1.anchor: اقترب الوعد الحق } يعني: القيامة، والواو زائدة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:97-99/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:97-99/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:97-99/r2.claim: The wāw is extra, since “it has drawn near” answers ḥattā (“until”).
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:97-99/r2.anchor: والواو زائدة؛ لأن " اقترب " جواب " حتى "

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:97-99/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:97-99/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:97-99/r3.claim: Their eyes stare fixedly and scarcely blink from the terror of that Day.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:97-99/r3.anchor: ذاهبة لا تكاد تطرف من هول ذلك اليوم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:97-99/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:97-99/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:97-99/r4.claim: They confess that, in worldly life, they had been heedless of this Day.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:97-99/r4.anchor: { يا ويلنا قد كنا في غفلة من هذا } في الدنيا عن هذا اليوم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:97-99/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:97-99/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:97-99/r5.claim: Their wrongdoing consisted of associating partners with God and denying the messengers.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p345/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p345/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p345/r1.claim: The approaching true promise is the second blast of the Trumpet.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p345/r1.anchor: قوله: {واقترب الوعد الحق} [الأنبياء: 97] يعني النفخة الآخرة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p345/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p345/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p345/r2.claim: The disbelievers' eyes stare toward answering the caller to Jerusalem.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p345/r2.anchor: {فإذا هي شاخصة أبصار الذين كفروا} [الأنبياء: 97] إلى إجابة الداعي إلى بيت المقدس.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p345/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p345/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p345/r3.claim: Their confession of heedlessness refers to their denial of the Hour.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p345/r3.anchor: {يا ويلنا} [الأنبياء: 97] يقولون: {قد كنا في غفلة من هذا} [الأنبياء: 97] يعنون تكذيبهم بالساعة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p345/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p345/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p345/r4.claim: They admit that they wronged themselves.

QASHANI:21:96-100/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:21:96-100/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:21:96-100/r3.claim: The true promise is the minor resurrection at death; the veiled stare in horror and admit their wrongdoing and shortcomings.
QASHANI:21:96-100/r3.anchor: { واقترب الوعد الحق } من وقوع القيامة الصغرى بالموت، فحينئذ شخصت أبصار المحجوبين

ELMALILI:21:92-100/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:92-100/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:92-100/r8.claim: The true promise draws near when the signs of the Resurrection appear and the Day of Judgment approaches.
ELMALILI:21:92-100/r8.anchor: yani kıyamet alâmetleri zuhur edip hesap gününün tekarrub ettiği vakit

ELMALILI:21:92-100/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:21:92-100/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:21:92-100/r9.claim: Disbelievers’ eyes bulge in terror; Elmalılı identifies them as those who rejected these signs and damaged the structure of communal unity, and who then confess negligence and injustice.
ELMALILI:21:92-100/r9.anchor: o küfredenlerin -bunlara inanmayıp bünyân-ı vahdeti rahnedar eden o nankör kâfirlerin- gözleri fırlamış

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:97/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:97/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:97/r1.claim: The approaching, unfailing promise means the Day of Resurrection; Gog and Magog's emergence signals its nearness and reinforces the previous verse.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:97/r1.anchor: Yaklaştığı bildirilen “şaşmaz sözün gerçekleşmesi”nden maksat kıyamet olayıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:97/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:97/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:97/r2.claim: The image of disbelievers' eyes staring out conveys the event's severity and people's astonishment and helplessness before the Resurrection.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:97/r2.anchor: “Bir de bakarsın ki inkârcıların gözleri yerinden fırlamış!” anlamındaki cümle de olayın şiddetini ve insanların kıyamet olayı karşısındaki şaşkınlığını, aczini ifade eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:97/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:97/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:97/r3.claim: With no return possible, disbelievers regret what they did and condemn themselves: prophets had repeatedly warned them of Resurrection and judgment, yet they denied them without excuse and admit their wrongdoing.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:97/r3.anchor: bütün peygamberler kıyametin kopacağını ve hesap gününün geleceğini haber vermiş oldukları halde onlar hiçbir mazeretleri olmaksızın kıyameti, dolayısıyla peygamberleri yalanlamışlardır

BAQILLANI:v1p274/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p274/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p274/r3.claim: Some locate Qurʾānic inimitability in badiʿ devices or listed forms of eloquence; Bāqillānī distinguishes learnable techniques, which cannot prove inimitability, from rhetorical qualities inaccessible to learning and practice.
BAQILLANI:v1p274/r3.anchor: ومن الناس من زعم انه يأخذ ذلك من هذه الوجوه التي عددناها في هذا الفصل

BAQILLANI:v1p274/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p274/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p274/r4.claim: Simile is a recognized form of eloquence, but it is not independently miraculous: Ibn al-Muʿtazz also composed striking, almost magical similes.
BAQILLANI:v1p274/r4.anchor: وأنت تجد في شعر ابن المعتز من التشبيه البديع الذي يشبه السحر

BAQILLANI:v1p274/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p274/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p274/r5.claim: He accepts that inimitability may lie in sustaining the highest eloquence across every subject and connecting the whole discourse with exceptional artistry.
BAQILLANI:v1p274/r5.anchor: إذا أتى في كل معنى يتفق في كلامه بالطبقة العالية ثم كان ما يصل به كلامه بعضه ببعض

BAQILLANI:v1p274/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p274/r6.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p274/r6.claim: No isolated device—an oath, simile, paronomasia, or antithesis—constitutes Qurʾānic inimitability without the composition that joins it to the surrounding discourse.
BAQILLANI:v1p274/r6.anchor: إنما ننكر أن يقول قائل إن بعض هذه الوجوه بانفرادها قد حصل فيه الإعجاز

BURHAN:v3p189/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p189/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p189/r10.claim: When the true promise comes, the disbelievers regret their former negligence, but their belief will not benefit them because this is among the signs of the Hour.
BURHAN:v3p189/r10.anchor: المعنى حتى إذا كان ذلك ندم الذين كفروا ولم ينفعهم إيمانهم لأنه من الآيات والاشراط

BURHAN:v3p275/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p275/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p275/r5.claim: The phrasing فإذا هي شاخصة أبصار الذين كفروا retains the pronoun and marks disbelievers as the ones whose eyes are fixed; omitting هي would lose that particularizing force.
BURHAN:v3p275/r5.anchor: وكان يستغنى عن الضمير لأن هذا لا يفيد اختصاص الذين كفروا بالشخوص

BURHAN:v3p395/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p395/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p395/r1.claim: The section explains apparent negation where a description is incomplete or its result absent, so wording denies the full or beneficial state rather than every outward act.
BURHAN:v3p395/r1.anchor: لأنه عدم كمال وصفه أو لانتفاء ثمرته

BURHAN:v4p419/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p419/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p419/r3.claim: Zarkashi lists min in the two phrases about hearts hardened from God's remembrance and being unaware of this as meaning ʿan, about or away from.
BURHAN:v4p419/r3.anchor: الثامن بمعنى عن نحو ﴿ فويل للقاسية قلوبهم من ذكر الله ﴾

BURHAN:v4p419/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p419/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p419/r4.claim: An alternative analysis takes min in both phrases as marking the starting point.

BURHAN:v4p419/r14.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p419/r14.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p419/r14.claim: Basran grammarians require extra min to precede an indefinite and occur in negation, prohibition or a question; some treat a positive conditional clause like negation.
BURHAN:v4p419/r14.anchor: الثالث عشر الزائدة ولها شرطان عند البصريين إن تدخل على نكرة وأن يكون الكلام نفيا

ITQAN:v2p552/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p552/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p552/r1.claim: The pronoun of affair, also called the pronoun of the unknown, departs from ordinary syntax in five ways: it anticipates its clause, takes a sentence explanation, has no dependent, is governed only by a subject or its abrogator, and stays singular.
ITQAN:v2p552/r1.anchor: ويسمى ضمير المجهول قال في المغني خالف القياس من خمسة أوجه

ITQAN:v2p552/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p552/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p552/r2.claim: The pronoun first leaves the matter vague and then explains it, magnifying the information that follows.
ITQAN:v2p552/r2.anchor: وفائدته الدلالة على تعظيم المخبر عنه وتفخيمه بأن يذكر أولا مبهما ثم يفسر

ITQAN:v2p517/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p517/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p517/r1.claim: In “we were heedless of this,” من means “about” or “concerning” (عن).
ITQAN:v2p517/r1.anchor: وعن نحو ﴿ قد كنا في غفلة من هذا ﴾ أي عنه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p265/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p265/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p265/r1.claim: Al-ḥaqq means what is sound and correct, opposite falsehood; ḥaqīqa is the true outcome of a matter, and ḥaqqa means became due.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p265/r1.anchor: الحق : الصواب والصحيح ، وضده : الباطل . والحقيقة : ما يصير إليه حق الأمر

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p265/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p265/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p265/r2.claim: The verb ḥāqqa describes disputants each claiming truth; when one prevails, ḥaqqahu or aḥaqqahu is used, as is iḥtaqqū for mutual claims.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p265/r2.anchor: وحاق فلان فلانا : إذا خاصمه وادعى كل واحد منهما الحق

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p265/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p265/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p265/r3.claim: Al-ḥāqqa names the Resurrection because it befalls all; ḥiqqa names a camel old enough to be ridden, and ḥuqāq is its plural.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p265/r3.anchor: والحاقة : القيامة ، لأنها تحق بكل . والحقة : من أولاد الإبل

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p265/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p265/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p265/r4.claim: The familiar box is called ḥuqqa, plural ḥuqaq; ḥaqḥaqa is the hardest, most exhausting pace for a rider’s back.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p265/r4.anchor: والحقة : معروفة ، والجمع : حقق . والحقحقة : أرفع السير وأتعبه للظهر

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p265/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p265/r5.speaker: مطرف بن عبد الله
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p265/r5.claim: Muṭarrif’s verse witnesses ḥaqḥaqa as exhausting travel, contrasting it with moderation as the best course.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p265/r5.anchor: قال مطرف بن عبد الله : إن خير الأمور أوساطها ، وإن شر السير الحقحقة

FARRA:v2p212/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p212/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p212/r1.claim: هي can be an ʿimād, with هو possible in its place; feminine agreement reflects أبصار, while masculine agreement is possible for the support pronoun, as in the cited Qurʾanic examples and Arab speech.
FARRA:v2p212/r1.anchor: تكون (هي) عمادا يصلح في موضعها (هو) فتكون كقوله: (إنه أنا الله العزيز الحكيم)

FARRA:v2p212/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p212/r2.speaker: بعضهم
FARRA:v2p212/r2.claim: An anonymous verse uses هو as an ʿimād, supporting Farrāʾ's analysis.
FARRA:v2p212/r2.anchor: وسمعت بعض العرب يقول: كان مرة وهو ينفع الناس أحسابهم فجعل (هو) عمادا.

FARRA:v2p212/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p212/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p212/r3.claim: Alternatively, هي refers to the eyes and أبصار then makes the referent explicit, like a poetic line that first refers to a woman by pronoun and then names her.
FARRA:v2p212/r3.anchor: وإن شئت جعلت (هي) للأبصار كنيت عنها ثم أظهرت الأبصار لتفسرها

FARRA:v2p212/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p212/r4.speaker: بعضهم
FARRA:v2p212/r4.claim: An anonymous poetic line witnesses the use of the support pronoun هو.
FARRA:v2p212/r4.anchor:
وأنشدني بعضهم:
بثوب ودينار وشاة ودرهم ... فهل هو مرفوع بما هاهنا راس

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p288#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p288#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p288#5/r1.claim: The true promise that has drawn near is the Day of Resurrection.

NAHHAS:v3p80/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p80/r1.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v3p80/r1.claim: Al-Kisa'i allows the poetic clause beginning وانتحى to serve as the answer to إذا; the line is cited as a syntactic parallel.
NAHHAS:v3p80/r1.anchor: المعنى عنده انتحى وأجاز الكسائي أن يكون جواب إذا

NAHHAS:v3p80/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p80/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p80/r2.claim: Abu Ishaq supplies an omitted قالوا before يا ويلنا, an interpretation al-Nahhas calls good and supports with the frequent omission of reported speech in the Qur'an.
NAHHAS:v3p80/r2.anchor: وهذا قول أبي إسحاق وهو قول حسن

SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r1.claim: Best, هي is a pronoun of the affair; شاخصة is the fronted predicate and أبصار the delayed subject, with the full sentence explaining the pronoun, as Basran grammarians require.
SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r1.anchor: فيه أوجه أحدها: وهو الأجود أن تكون " هي " ضمير القصة، و " شاخصة " خبر مقدم،

SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r2.speaker: الكوفيون
SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r2.claim: On the Kufan account, شاخصة is the subject and أبصار is a subject-like agent filling the predicate position; a single verb-like word can explain the pronoun of the affair.
SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r2.anchor: الثاني: أن تكون " شاخصة " مبتدأ، و " أبصار " فاعل سد مسد الخبر، وهذا يتمشى على رأي الكوفيين

SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari calls هي an ambiguous pronoun clarified by أبصار, comparable to الذين ظلموا followed by أسروا.
SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r3.anchor: الثالث: قال الزمخشري: " هي " ضمير مبهم توضحه الأبصار وتفسره،

SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r4.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ takes هي as referring to أبصار, advanced because context points to it; he adduces the cited poem as evidence for the pronoun's placement.
SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r4.anchor: قلت: وهذا هو قول الفراء؛ فإنه قال: " هي " ضمير الأبصار تقدمت لدلالة الكلام ومجيء ما يفسرها ". وأنشد شاهدا على ذلك:/ 3362 فلا وأبيها لا تقول حليلتي

SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r5.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ also allows هي as a separating pronoun (عماد), since هو could replace it, citing the poem as evidence.
SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r5.anchor: الرابع: أن تكون " هي " عمادا، وهو قول الفراء أيضا، قال: " لأنه يصلح موضعها " هو " وأنشد: 3363 بثوب ودينار وشاة ودرهم

SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r6.speaker: الكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r6.claim: This separating-pronoun analysis relies on one al-Kisāʾī view that permits the separator before a fronted predicate, as in هو خير منك زيد.
SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r6.anchor: وهذا لا يتمشى إلا على أحد قولي الكسائي: وهو أنه يجيز تقدم الفصل مع الخبر المقدم

SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r7.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r7.claim: The Shaykh cites the analysis هو القائم زيد with زيد as subject and القائم as predicate, placing هو as a separator.
SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r7.anchor: وقال الشيخ: " أجاز هو القائم زيد، على أن " زيدا " هو المبتدأ

SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r8.claim: The author questions the Shaykh's example because fronting the predicate is impossible when both nouns are definite; the verse instead has أبصار الذين كفروا هي شاخصة, with the separator moving alongside the fronted predicate, a view that allows it before a non-near-definite noun.
SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r8.anchor: قلت: وفي هذا التمثيل [نظر]؛ لأن تقديم الخبر هنا ممتنع لا ستوائهما في التعريف،

SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r9.speaker: الثعلبي
SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r9.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī makes هي a subject with an omitted predicate meaning that the Hour is present, then starts a separate clause شاخصة أبصار; the author calls this very remote and rhetorically tangled.
SAMIN-DURR:21:97/r9.anchor: ذكره الثعلبي. وهو بعيد جدا لتنافر التركيب، وهو التعقيد عند علماء البيان.

SAMIN-DURR:21:97#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:97#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:97#2/r1.claim: ويلنا is governed by an omitted verb of saying, either as the answer to حتى إذا or as a circumstantial phrase from الذين كفروا.
SAMIN-DURR:21:97#2/r1.anchor: قوله: { يويلنا } معمول لقول محذوف، وفي هذا القول المحذوف وجهان، أحدهما: أنه جواب " حتى إذا "

SAMIN-DURR:21:97#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:97#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:21:97#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari gives the omitted saying as a circumstantial phrase from الذين كفروا.
SAMIN-DURR:21:97#2/r2.anchor: والثاني: في محل نصب على الحال من " الذين كفروا " ، قاله الزمخشري.

ZAJJAJ:v3p405/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p405/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ZAJJAJ:v3p405/r7.claim: Some object that the waw cannot be omitted before the report of what the people say.

ZAJJAJ:v3p405/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p405/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p405/r8.claim: The Basran reply supplies an omitted قالوا: after the opening of Gog and Magog and the approach of the true promise, they say their confession.
ZAJJAJ:v3p405/r8.anchor: والجواب عند البصريين قوله: (يا ويلنا قد كنا في غفلة من هذا)

ZAJJAJ:v3p405/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p405/r9.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v3p405/r9.claim: Tafsir identifies the emergence of Gog and Magog as one of the signs of the Hour.
ZAJJAJ:v3p405/r9.anchor: وجاء في التفسير أن خروج يأجوج ومأجوج من أعلام الساعة

ASAD-NOTES:21:94#n95/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:21:94#n95/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:21:94#n95/r1.claim: Asad reads the deniers' admission of heedlessness as deliberate and inexcusable because prophets had warned humanity of resurrection and judgment.
ASAD-NOTES:21:94#n95/r1.anchor: deliberately and without any excuse, since all the prophets had warned man of the Day of Resurrection and Judgment

ASAD-NOTES:21:94#n95/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:21:94#n95/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:21:94#n95/r2.claim: Asad's added phrase “bent on” marks intent in “those who deny the truth,” paralleling his interpretation of alladhina kafaru in 2:6.
ASAD-NOTES:21:94#n95/r2.anchor: The words "bent on" interpolated by me within brackets indicate intent, similar to the preceding expression alladhina kafaru

NASHR:v2p83/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p83/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p83/r1.claim: When pausing on feminine tāʾ, use fatḥ if the preceding letter is among ten specified letters; after alif fatḥ is agreed, and after the other nine it is the preferred rule. شاخصة is listed under ṣād.
NASHR:v2p83/r1.anchor: الذي يوقف عليه بالفتح، وذلك إن كان قبل الهاء حرف من عشرة أحرف

NASHR:v2p83/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p83/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p83/r2.claim: The ten-letter class is ḥāʾ, ʿayn, alif, and the seven emphatics; the text lists counts and examples for each, including شاخصة among ṣād forms.

NASHR:v2p83/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p83/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p83/r3.claim: Tawrāt, taqāt, marḍāt, mazjāt, and mishkāt are excluded from this class; their alif is imāla in connected and paused reading under the preceding rule.
NASHR:v2p83/r3.anchor: فليس من هذا الباب، بل من الباب قبله تمال ألفه وصلا ووقفا

NASHR:v2p83/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p83/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p83/r4.claim: For the four-letter class hamza, kāf, hāʾ, and rāʾ, imāla applies when a silent yāʾ or kasra precedes; otherwise use fatḥ, and an intervening sukūn does not block it.
NASHR:v2p83/r4.anchor: وذلك إذا كان قبل الهاء حرف من أربعة أحرف

ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r1.claim: The verb means came near; another view says it expresses nearness more emphatically than qaruba.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r1.anchor: أي قرب وقيل هو أبلغ في القرب من قرب

ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r2.claim: The true promise is the resurrection, reckoning, and recompense after the second trumpet blast, rather than the first; the clause follows the opening of Gog and Magog.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r2.anchor: ما بعد النفخة الثانية من البعث والحساب والجزاء لا النفخة الأولى

ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r3.claim: A long report in Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Majah places Gog and Magog after Jesus kills the Dajjal: they die by a divine affliction, then birds and rain cleanse the earth, abundance returns, a wind takes every believer, and the Hour comes upon the wicked.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r3.anchor: فقد أخرج مسلم وأبو داود والترمذي والنسائي وابن ماجه من حديث طويل إن الله تعالى يوحي إلى عيسى عليه السلام بعد أن يقتل الدجال

ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r4.claim: A report related by Ahmad and others compares the Hour after Gog and Magog perish to a full-term pregnancy whose delivery surprises the family by night or day.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r4.anchor: وجاء من حديث رواه أحمد وجماعة أن الساعة بعد أن يهلك يأجوج ومأجوج كالحامل المتم لا يدري أهلها حتى تفجأهم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports that the Prophet said that if a horse survived the emergence of Gog and Magog, its foal would not be ridden before the Hour, stressing its nearness.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r5.anchor: ذكر لنا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لو نجت فرس عند خروجهم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r6.claim: The conditional answer uses surprise إذا, which can replace the linking fāʾ for a nominal clause; using both here strengthens the link.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r6.anchor: وإذا للمفاجأة وهي تسد مسد الفاء الجزائية

ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r7.claim: The standard parsing makes هي the pronoun of the matter, شاخصة the fronted predicate, and أبصار the delayed subject; the sentence then explains that pronoun.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r7.anchor: والضمير للقصة والشأن وهو مبتدأ و ( شاخصة ) خبر مقدم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r8.speaker: بعض الكوفيين
ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r8.claim: Some Kufans allow the pronoun of the matter to take a single-word predicate, which would permit شاخصة to be predicate and أبصار its subject; the author rejects this parsing under the usual rule.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r8.anchor: وأجاز بعض الكوفيين كونه مفردا فيجوز ما ذكر عنده

ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r9.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r9.claim: Al-Farra takes هي as a pronoun for the eyes, clarified later in its predicate; Ibn Malik and others allow such a pronoun to precede its referent.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p92#2/r9.anchor: وعن الفراء أن هي ضمير الأبصار فهو ضمير مبهم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r1.claim: The phrase هو الجد حتى تفضل العين أختها is cited as poetic evidence for a pronoun whose referent follows it.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r1.anchor: هو الجد حتى تفضل العين أختها

ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r2.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r2.claim: Al-Farra allows a later clarifier outside the pronoun's predicate when context indicates the referent, citing a line about Malik ibn Abi Ka'b.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r2.anchor: بل نقل عن الفراء أنه متى دل الكلام على المرجح وذكره بعده ما يفسره

ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r3.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r3.claim: Al-Farra also calls هي a separative or support pronoun and cites poetry; this works only with al-Kisa'i's allowance for placing it before the predicate while the predicate precedes the subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r3.anchor: ونقل عنه أيضا أن ( هي ) ضمير فصل وعماد يصلح موضعه

ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r4.speaker: الثعلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r4.claim: Al-Tha'labi makes the clause end at فإذا هي, understood as the Hour appearing or occurring, then begins شاخصة أبصار; the author calls this strained and discordant.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r4.anchor: الكلام قد تم عند قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r5.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r5.claim: Another reported parsing makes اقترب the conditional answer and treats the waw as extra, a view attributed to al-Farra in Majma al-Bayan.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r5.anchor: الواو سيف خطيب ونقل ذلك في مجمع البيان عن الفراء

ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r6.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj says Basran grammarians do not allow an extra waw; they take the answer as an elided saying, يا ويلنا.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r6.anchor: عن الزجاج أن البصريين لا يجوزون زيادة الواو

ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r7.claim: If اقترب is taken as the answer, the cry is also introduced by an implicit they-said; يقولون يا ويلنا may be a circumstantial clause or a fresh sentence.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r7.anchor: قدر القول ههنا أيضا وجعله حالا من الموصول يقولون

ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r8.claim: Their eyes stare upward with raised lids and without blinking, from the terror of the Day of Judgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r8.anchor: شخوص الأبصار رفع أجفانها إلى قوق من دون أن تطرف

ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r9.claim: Their cry for woe expresses regret, as if summoning woe to arrive because its time has come.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r9.anchor: من نداء الويل التحسر وكأنهم قالوا

ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r10.claim: They say they had been wholly heedless of the resurrection and return to God for recompense; another view specifies that they did not know this day was real.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r10.anchor: الذي دهمنا من البعث والرجوع إليه عز وجل للجزاء

ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r11.claim: They retract the claim of heedlessness: warnings had reached them, but they wronged themselves by abandoning or denying the signs and warnings, exposing themselves to eternal punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p93/r11.anchor: ظالمين بترك الآيات والنذر مكذبين بها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r1.claim: The true promise is the Resurrection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r1.anchor: {واقترب الوعد الحق} يعني القيامة، قال الفراء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r2.speaker: الفراء وجماعة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and others treat the wāw as extra, so the promise draws near after Gog and Magog are released; they compare the wording with the wāw in Ṣāffāt 37:103.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r2.anchor: قال الفراء وجماعة: الواو في قوله واقترب [مقحمة فمعناه حتى إذا فتحت يأجوج ومأجوج اقترب] (2) الوعد الحق،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r3.speaker: حذيفة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r3.claim: A report from Ḥudhayfah says that if someone acquired a young horse after Gog and Magog emerged, he would not ride it before the Hour.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r3.anchor: ما روي عن حذيفة قال: لو أن رجلا اقتنى فلوا بعد خروج يأجوج ومأجوج لم يركبه حتى تقوم الساعة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r5.claim: One analysis takes “it” as a pronoun for the eyes, then repeats “eyes” for clarification.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r5.anchor: أحدها: أنها كناية عن الأبصار. ثم أظهر الأبصار بيانا،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r6.claim: A second analysis treats “it” as a supporting pronoun, as in the construction cited from Hajj 22:46.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r6.anchor: والثاني: أن "هي" تكون عمادا كقوله: {فإنها لا تعمى الأبصار} (الحج:46) .

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r7.claim: A third analysis ends the first clause at “it is,” meaning the event is present, then fronts the predicate: the unbelievers’ eyes are fixed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r7.anchor: ثم ابتدأ: {شاخصة أبصار الذين كفروا} على تقديم الخبر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r8.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r8.claim: Al-Kalbī says the disbelievers’ eyes are frozen open, scarcely blinking from the terror and horror of that day.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r8.anchor: قال الكلبي: شخصت أبصار الكفار فلا تكاد تطرف من شدة ذلك اليوم وهوله،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r9.claim: The unbelievers lament that they had been heedless of that day; they admit they were wrongdoers by worshipping the wrong objects.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p355#2/r9.anchor: يقولون، {يا ويلنا قد كنا في غفلة من هذا} اليوم،

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:97-98/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:97-98/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:97-98/r1.claim: The true promise that has drawn near is the Resurrection.

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:97-98/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:97-98/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:97-98/r2.claim: “Then suddenly” is the conditional answer; إذا of sudden occurrence can stand for the answer’s fāʾ, while their combination strengthens the link, as at 30:36.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:97-98/r2.anchor: جواب الشرط و «إذا» للمفاجأة تسد مسد الفاء الجزائية كقوله تعالى:

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:97-98/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:97-98/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:97-98/r3.claim: The pronoun may refer to the whole situation or be an unspecified pronoun explained by “the eyes.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:97-98/r3.anchor: والضمير للقصة أو مبهم يفسره الأبصار.

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:97-98/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:97-98/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:97-98/r4.claim: “Woe to us” has an understood verb of saying and functions circumstantially with the relative clause.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:97-98/r4.anchor: مقدر بالقول واقع موقع الحال من الموصول.

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:97-98/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:97-98/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:97-98/r5.claim: They confess that they had not known this promise was true.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:97-98/r5.anchor: قد كنا فى غفلة من هذا } لم نعلم أنه حق.

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:97-98/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:97-98/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:97-98/r6.claim: They acknowledge wronging themselves by neglecting reflection and paying no heed to warnings.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:97-98/r6.anchor: بل كنا ظلمين } لأنفسنا بالإخلال بالنظر وعدم الاعتداد بالنذر.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r10.claim: The true promise is the resurrection of the dead, which closely approaches and corresponds to what will actually occur.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r10.anchor: وهو حشر الأموات الذي يطابقه الواقع , إذا وجد قربا عظيما

BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r11.claim: The form iftaʿala conveys an intensified nearness, likened to the Hour’s closeness when a pregnant woman is about to deliver.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r11.anchor: دلت صيغة ( افتعل ) على شدة القرب كما في الحديث أن الساعة إذ ذاك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r12.claim: A hadith is cited as comparing the Hour’s nearness at that time to a pregnant woman near term; no authority or grading is supplied here.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r12.anchor: كما في الحديث أن الساعة إذ ذاك مثل الحامل المتم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r13.claim: The sudden ifā may answer the conditional ifā directly and stand in place of fa; when fa also appears with it, the link between condition and result is reinforced.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r13.anchor: ويجوز وهو أقرب أن تكون إذا هذه الفجائية هي جواب إذا الشرطية

BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r14.claim: The disbelievers’ eyes are fixed and unblinking when the horrors they never expected appear before them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r14.anchor: واقفة جامدة لا تطرف لما دهمهم من الشدة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r15.claim: Their cry means that woe has arrived and become their companion, with no other helper or rescuer to call.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r15.anchor: حضرنا الويل فهو نديمنا فلا مدعو لنا غيره

BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r16.claim: They say that in worldly life they were heedless of resurrection because they denied it.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r16.anchor: أي مبتدئة من اعتقاد هذا البعث فكنا نكذب به فعمتنا الغفلة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r17.claim: They correct their claim of heedlessness: the evidence was unmistakable, but they wronged themselves by refusing reflection, signs, and the messengers’ teaching.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p111/r17.anchor: حيث أعرضنا عن تأمل دلائله , والنظر في مخايله , وتقبل كلام الرسل فيه

DURR-FULL:v5p674/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p674/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p674/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports a Prophetic account of the Night Journey: Abraham, Moses, and Jesus defer knowledge of the Hour, whose exact onset God alone knows.
DURR-FULL:v5p674/r2.anchor: عن ابن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: لقيت ليلة أسري بي إبراهيم وموسى وعيسى فتذاكروا أمر الساعة فردوا أمرهم إلى إبراهيم

DURR-FULL:v5p674/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p674/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p674/r3.claim: In the same report, Jesus says the Dajjāl will emerge and he will kill him; stones and trees will call Muslims to kill unbelievers hiding beneath them.
DURR-FULL:v5p674/r3.anchor: وفيما عهد إلي ربي أن الدجال خارج ومعي قضيبان فإذا رآني ذاب كما يذوب الرصاص فيهلكه الله إذا رآني حتى أن الحجر والشجر يقول: يا مسلم إن تحتي كافرا فتعال فاقتله

DURR-FULL:v5p674/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p674/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p674/r4.claim: After the Dajjāl’s people are destroyed, the report says God kills them, foulness covers the earth, and rain carries their bodies into the sea.
DURR-FULL:v5p674/r4.anchor: ثم يرجع الناس يشكونهم فأدعو الله عليهم فيهلكهم ويميتهم حتى تجري الأرض من نتن ريحهم وينزل الله المطر فيجترف أجسادهم حتى يقذفهم في البحر

DURR-FULL:v5p674/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p674/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p674/r5.claim: The report compares the Hour’s sudden arrival to a full-term pregnant woman whose family cannot know whether labor will begin by night or day.
DURR-FULL:v5p674/r5.anchor: وفيما عهد إلي ربي إذا كان ذلك أن الساعة كالحامل المتم لا يدري أهلها متى تفجأهم بولادتها ليلا أو نهارا

DURR-FULL:v5p674/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p674/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p674/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says he found this account of Gog and Magog and the approaching true promise confirmed in these verses.
DURR-FULL:v5p674/r6.anchor: قال ابن مسعود: فوجدت تصديق ذلك في كتاب الله: {حتى إذا فتحت يأجوج ومأجوج وهم من كل حدب ينسلون واقترب الوعد الحق}

DURR-FULL:v5p678/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p678/r1.speaker: حذيفة
DURR-FULL:v5p678/r1.claim: Hudhayfa says that after Gog and Magog emerge, a man who acquires a foal will not ride it before the Hour.
DURR-FULL:v5p678/r1.anchor: عن حذيفة رضي الله عنه قال: لو أن رجلا اقتنى فلوا بعد خروج يأجوج ومأجوج

DURR-FULL:v5p678/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p678/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p678/r2.claim: The Prophet says people will still perform pilgrimage and minor pilgrimage to the House after Gog and Magog emerge.
DURR-FULL:v5p678/r2.anchor: عن أبي سعيد رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ليحجن هذا البيت وليعتمرن بعد خروج يأجوج ومأجوج

DURR-FULL:v5p678/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p678/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v5p678/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the approaching true promise as the Day of Resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v5p678/r3.anchor: عن ابن زيد {واقترب الوعد الحق} قال: اقترب يوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v5p678/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p678/r4.speaker: الربيع
DURR-FULL:v5p678/r4.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says the Hour has already come upon them.
DURR-FULL:v5p678/r4.anchor: عن الربيع {واقترب الوعد الحق} قال: قامت عليهم الساعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r1.claim: Initial ḥattā need not mark a regular temporal endpoint; with an independent clause it links statements and marks the speaker’s progression to a new purpose, as in Labīd’s Muʿallaqah.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r1.anchor: فأما ( حتى ) الابتدائية فإن وجود معنى الغاية معها في مواقعها غير منضبط ولا مطرد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r2.claim: The use of ḥattā in 2:214 likewise introduces what arose from the distress, not a literal endpoint at which the Messenger spoke.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r2.anchor: وفي قوله تعالى : { وزلزلوا حتى يقول الرسول والذين آمنوا معه متى نصر الله }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r3.claim: The scene follows the opening of Gog and Magog and the nearness of the promise to convey how quickly the disbelievers’ shock arrives.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r3.anchor: وقد مثلت حالة الكافرين في ذلك الحين بأبلغ تمثيل وأشده وقعا في نفس السامع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r4.claim: The fa and idhā convey sudden, immediate arrival without interval; the pronoun of the story gives a vague advance notice that the following words resolve.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r4.anchor: ثم بتصدير الجملة بحرف المفاجأة والمجازاة الذي يفيد الحصول دفعة بلا تدرج ولا مهلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r5.claim: Shukhūṣ is a fixed, unmoving stare, as when someone is stunned.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r5.anchor: والشخوص : إحداد البصر دون تحرك كما يقع للمبهوت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r6.claim: The phrase is quoted speech with an omitted verb: they say, Woe to us, at that moment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r6.anchor: مقول قول محذوف كما هو ظاهر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r7.claim: Fī depicts heedlessness as enveloping them like a container surrounds its contents; it is heedlessness toward evidence for resurrection and recompense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r7.anchor: على تمكن الغفلة منهم حتى كأنها محيطة بهم إحاطة الظرف بالمظروف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r8.claim: Their cry is a self-directed imprecation prompted by the calamity that has overtaken them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r8.anchor: دعاء على أنفسهم من شدة ما لحقهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r9.claim: Bal retracts the claim of heedlessness: they had been warned, but wronged themselves through stubborn opposition and turning away.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r9.anchor: للإضراب الإبطالي ، أي ما كنا في غفلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r10.claim: This refers collectively to the events of resurrection, reckoning, and recompense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p151/r10.anchor: هو مجموع تلك الأحوال من الحشر والحساب والجزاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p99#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p99#2/r2.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p99#2/r2.claim: One group makes iqtaraba al-waʿd the answer to ḥattā and treats wāw as extra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p99#2/r2.anchor: واختلف هنا في الجواب، فقالت فرقة الجواب قوله اقترب الوعد والواو زائدة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p99#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p99#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p99#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj and others make yā waylanā the answer, supplying ‘they said’; this view does not treat wāw as extra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p99#2/r3.anchor: وقالت فرقة منها الزجاج وغيره الجواب في قوله يا ويلنا التقدير قالوا يا ويلنا وليست الواو بزائدة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p99#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p99#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p99#2/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya makes fa-idhā hiya shākhiṣa the answer; it expresses the return they denied, whose occurrence they cannot escape.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p99#2/r4.anchor: والذي أقول إن الجواب في قوله فإذا هي شاخصة وهذا هو المعنى الذي قصد ذكره لأنه رجوعهم الذي كانوا يكذبون به وحرم عليهم امتناعه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r7.claim: The certain promise that has drawn near is the Day of Resurrection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r7.anchor: وقوله تعالى: واقترب الوعد الحق يريد يوم القيامة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r8.speaker: رُوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r8.claim: A report says someone may prepare a foal after Gog and Magog appear but will not benefit from it before the Hour begins.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r8.anchor: وروي في الحديث «أن الرجل ليتخذ الفلو بعد يأجوج ومأجوج فلا يبلغ منفعته حتى تقوم الساعة»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r9.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r9.claim: Sībawayh analyzes hiya as the pronoun of the affair, roughly ‘then the event is eyes staring.’
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r9.anchor: مذهب سيبويه أنها ضمير القصة كأنه قال فإذا القصة أو الحادثة شاخصة أبصار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r10.speaker: الفراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r10.claim: Al-Farrāʾ allows hiya to anticipate the eyes, which the subsequent words explain, and adduces Arabic poetry as evidence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r10.anchor: وجوز الفراء أن تكون ضمير الأبصار تقدمت لدلالة الكلام ويجيء ما يفسرها وأنشد على ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r11.speaker: الفراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r11.claim: The poem ‘fa-lā wa-abīhā ...’ is cited to support al-Farrāʾ’s anticipatory pronoun construction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r11.anchor: فلا وأبيها لا تقول حليلتي ... ألا فرعني مالك بن أبي كعب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r12.claim: Staring eyes are fixed open without blinking, as happens from extreme fear, illness, or similar causes.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r12.anchor: والشخوص بالعين إحداد النظر دون أن يطرف، وذلك يعتري من الخوف المفرط أو علة أو نحوه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r13.claim: Their cry means they had been heedless of what they now see and recognize; they then realize they were unjust in persisting in unbelief and turning away.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p100/r13.anchor: وقوله: يا ويلنا تقديره يا ويلنا لقد كانت بنا غفلة عما وجدنا الآن وتبينا الآن من الحقائق ثم تركوا الكلام الأول ورجعوا إلى نقد ما كان يداخلهم من تعهد الكفر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r1.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r1.claim: Al-Farraʾ says “she” refers to the eyes, with “eyes” clarifying the pronoun; he cites a poetic example of a she-camel clarified after a pronoun.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r1.anchor: أحدها أن هي كناية عن الابصار والابصار تفسير لها كقول الشاعر لعمرو أبيها لا تقول ظعينتي ألا فرعني مالك بن أبي كعب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r2.claim: Al-Farraʾ also treats “she” as a separator or supporting pronoun replaceable by “he,” comparing 27:9 and 22:46 and citing a line of poetry.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r2.anchor: والثاني أن هي ضمير فصل وعماد ويصح في موضعها هو ومثله قول إنه أنا الله النمل 9 وقوله فانها لا تعمى الأبصار الحج 46 وأنشدوا بثوب ودينار وشاه ودرهم فهل هو مرفوع بما هاهنا رأس ذكرهما الفراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r3.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r3.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi says the clause may end at “she”: “there she is, standing before them,” after which “fixed” begins a new clause.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r3.anchor: والثالث أن يكون تمام الكلام عند قوله هي على معنى فاذا هي بارزة واقفة يعني من قربها كأنها آتية حاضرة ثم ابتدأ فقال شاخصة ذكره الثعلبي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r4.speaker: علي بن أحمد النيسابوري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r4.claim: ʿAli ibn Ahmad al-Nisaburi takes “she” as a pronoun for the whole event: the event is that the unbelievers' eyes are fixed on that day.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r4.anchor: والرابع أن هي كناية عن القصة والمعنى القصة أن ابصارهم شاخصة في ذلك اليوم ذكره علي بن أحمد النيسابوري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r5.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r5.claim: The commentators say the unbelievers' eyes stare in terror at the horror of the Resurrection.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r5.anchor: قال المفسرون تشخص ابصار الكفار من هول يوم القيامة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r6.claim: Their cry means they had been heedless of this in worldly life; “from this” means “about this.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r6.anchor: ويقولون يا ويلنا قد كنا أي في الدنيا في غفلة من هذا أي عن هذا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r7.claim: They confess that they wronged themselves through unbelief and disobedience.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p389/r7.anchor: بل كنا ظالمين أنفسنا بكفرنا ومعاصينا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p373/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p373/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p373/r1.claim: Nawwās ibn Samʿān reports the Prophet's warning about the Dajjal: he is a curly-haired young man with a floating eye, emerges between Syria and Iraq, and believers must stand firm.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p373/r1.anchor: ذكر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الدجال ذات غداة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p373/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p373/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p373/r2.claim: The Prophet says the Dajjal remains forty days, the first like a year, the next like a month, the next like a week, and the rest ordinary; believers should estimate prayer times during the year-long day.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p373/r2.anchor: قال: "أربعين يوما، يوم كسنة، ويوم كشهر، ويوم كجمعة، وسائر أيامه كأيامكم"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p373/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p373/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p373/r3.claim: The Dajjal travels as fast as wind-driven rain; those who accept him receive rain, crops, and thriving livestock, while those who reject him face famine and loss.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p373/r3.anchor: فيمر بالحي فيدعوهم فيستجيبون له، فيأمر السماء فتمطر، والأرض فتنبت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p373/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p373/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p373/r4.claim: He commands a ruined place to yield its treasures, which follow him like swarms of bees; he then kills a man and the man returns to him radiant.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p373/r4.anchor: ويمر بالخربة فيقول لها: أخرجي كنوزك، فتتبعه كنوزها كيعاسيب النحل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p373/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p373/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p373/r5.claim: The Prophet says Jesus will descend at the white minaret east of Damascus, pursue the Dajjal, and kill him at the eastern gate of Ludd.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p373/r5.anchor: فبينما هم على ذلك، إذ بعث الله عز وجل المسيح ابن مريم، فينزل عند المنارة (2) البيضاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p376/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p376/r4.speaker: كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p376/r4.claim: Kaʿb says that after news of Dhu al-Suwayqatayn, Jesus sends a vanguard of seven or eight hundred; a fragrant wind takes every believer, leaving people who mate like beasts as the Hour approaches.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p376/r4.anchor: فبينما الناس كذلك إذ أتاهم الصريخ أن ذا السويقتين يريده

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p376/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p376/r5.speaker: author
