IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p376/r5.claim: Ibn Kathīr regards this as one of Kaʿb al-Aḥbār's best accounts because authentic reports corroborate it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p376/r5.anchor: هذا من أحسن سياقات كعب الأحبار، لما شهد له من صحيح الأخبار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p376#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p376#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p376#2/r1.claim: Abū Saʿīd reports the Prophet saying that people will perform Hajj and ʿUmra at the Kaʿba after Gog and Magog emerge; al-Bukhārī alone transmits it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p376#2/r1.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "ليحجن هذا البيت، وليعتمرن بعد خروج يأجوج ومأجوج"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p376#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p376#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p376#2/r2.claim: The promised truth is the Day of Resurrection; once its terrors, earthquakes, and upheavals occur, the Hour will be imminent.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p376#2/r2.anchor: يعني: يوم القيامة، إذا وجدت هذه الأهوال والزلازل والبلابل، أزفت الساعة واقتربت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p376#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p376#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p376#2/r3.claim: At the sight of these terrible events, disbelievers' eyes stare in shock and they cry woe, admitting they were heedless in worldly life and wronged themselves; the confession then cannot benefit them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p376#2/r3.anchor: أي: من شدة ما يشاهدونه من الأمور العظام: {يا ويلنا} أي: يقولون:

JISHUMI:v7p4887/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4887/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4887/r7.claim: Qaruba and iqtirāba have the same meaning.
JISHUMI:v7p4887/r7.anchor: والنسلان ضربان من المشي، نسل ينسل، وعسل يعسل، وقرب واقترب بمعنى.

JISHUMI:v7p4887/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4887/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4887/r8.claim: Shukhūṣ can mean a traveler leaving home, a troubling event that unsettles someone, travel from town to town, or a gaze fixed outward; the root also describes an arrow that passes above its target.
JISHUMI:v7p4887/r8.anchor: وشخوص المسافر: خروجه من منزله، وشخص به إذا أتاه ما يقلقه، كأنه رفع من الأرض، وشخص من بلد إلى بلد: خرج إليه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p135#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p135#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p135#2/r5.claim: Those decreed for destruction remain sealed in unbelief until punishment; only at Resurrection do they return and confess their heedlessness and wrongdoing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p135#2/r5.anchor: أن قوما عزم الله على إهلاكهم غير متصور أن يرجعوا وينيبوا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p136#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p136#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p136#2/r1.claim: The sudden إذا can stand in a conditional apodosis in place of the fāʾ; when both occur together, they link the result to the condition emphatically.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p136#2/r1.anchor: و {إذا } هي إذا المفاجأة ، وهي تقع في المجازاة سادة مسد الفاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p136#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p136#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p136#2/r2.claim: Using either “idhā hiya shākhiṣa” or “fa-hiya shākhiṣa” without the other particle would also be sound.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p136#2/r2.anchor: فإذا جاءت الفاء معها تعاونتا على وصل الجزاء بالشرط فيتأكد ولو قيل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p136#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p136#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p136#2/r3.claim: The pronoun hiyā is indefinite or ambiguous in reference, then explained and specified by “eyes,” as in the parallel wording about wrongdoers whispering.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p136#2/r3.anchor: ضمير مبهم توضحه الأبصار وتفسره ، كما فسر الذين ظلموا وأسروا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p136#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p136#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p136#2/r4.claim: Yā waylanā depends on an omitted “they say”; the saying is circumstantial to “those who disbelieved.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p136#2/r4.anchor: * يا ويلنا } متعلق بمحذوف تقديره : يقولون يا ويلنا ، ويقولون : في موضع الحال من الذين كفروا

MUQATIL:21:97-99/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:21:97-99/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:21:97-99/r1.claim: The true promise is the promise of resurrection, which will certainly occur.
MUQATIL:21:97-99/r1.anchor: يعنى وعد البعث أنه حق كائن

MUQATIL:21:97-99/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:21:97-99/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:21:97-99/r2.claim: “Staring” means open; the unbelievers will not blink at the wonders they see, which they denied in this life.
MUQATIL:21:97-99/r2.anchor: يعنى فاتحة { أبصار الذين كفروا } بالبعث لا يطرفون مما يرون

MUQATIL:21:97-99/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:21:97-99/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:21:97-99/r3.claim: On seeing the Day of Resurrection, the unbelievers admit they were heedless of it and wrong because messengers warned them but they denied it.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r1.claim: The true promise is the Resurrection.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r2.claim: The answer to idha is idha hiya, with sudden idha; sudden idha can stand in place of the fa in a recompense clause.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r2.anchor: وجواب اذا ﴿ فإذا هي ﴾ وهي إذا المفاجأة وهي تقع في المجازاة سادة مسد الفاء

NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r3.claim: When fa is also included after idha, the two particles jointly connect the answer to its condition and reinforce the link; the wording could instead say fa-hiya shakhisa or idha hiya shakhisa.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r3.anchor: فإذا جاءت الفاء معها تعاونتا على وصل الجزاء بالشرط فيتأكد

NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r4.claim: The pronoun hiya is indefinite or ambiguous until explained by al-absar.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r4.anchor: وهي ضمير مبهم يوضحه الابصار ويفسره

NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r5.claim: The disbelievers' eyes are fixed with lids raised, scarcely blinking from the terror they experience.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r5.anchor: ﴿ شاخصة أبصار الذين كفروا ﴾ أي مرتفعة الأجفان لا تكاد تطرف

NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r6.claim: The exclamation depends on an omitted verb meaning they say; the saying is circumstantial of the disbelievers.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r6.anchor: ﴿ يا ويلنا ﴾ متعلق بمحذوف تقديره يقولون يا ويلنا ويقولون حال من الذين كفروا

NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r7.claim: This refers to the Day of Resurrection.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r7.anchor: ﴿ قد كنا في غفلة من هذا ﴾ اليوم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r8.claim: They confess to wrongdoing by putting worship in a place where it did not belong.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p91#4/r8.anchor: ﴿ بل كنا ظالمين ﴾ بوضعنا العبادة في غير موضعها

QURTUBI-FULL:21:96-97/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:96-97/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:96-97/r9.claim: The true promise that has drawn near is the Resurrection.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:96-97/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:96-97/r10.speaker: الفراء والكسائي وغيرهما
QURTUBI-FULL:21:96-97/r10.claim: Al-Farra, al-Kisaʾi, and others treat the waw as extra: when Gog and Magog are opened, the true promise approaches, and fa-iqtaraba answers idhā.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:96-97/r10.anchor: وقال الفراء والكسائي وغيرهما: الواو زائدة مقحمة

QURTUBI-FULL:21:96-97/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:96-97/r11.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:21:96-97/r11.claim: Al-Farra cites poetry where waw is extra, and compares the Qur'anic phrase wa-tallahū lil-jabīn wa-nādaynāhu, understood as tallahū lil-jabīn nādaynāhu.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:96-97/r11.anchor:
وأنشد الفراء:
فلما أجزنا ساحة الحي وانتحى

QURTUBI-FULL:21:96-97/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:96-97/r12.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:21:96-97/r12.claim: Al-Kisaʾi allows fa-idhā hiya shākhiṣatun to answer idhā, with iqtaraba al-waʿd al-ḥaqq coordinated to the conditional verb.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:96-97/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:96-97/r13.speaker: البصريون والزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:21:96-97/r13.claim: The Basran grammarians, including al-Zajjaj, say the answer is omitted, with an estimate such as qālū yā waylanā; the author calls this a sound view.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:96-97/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:96-97/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:96-97/r14.claim: The omitted speech is supported by the common deletion of qālū, as in the verse about those who worship intermediaries and say they seek nearness to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:96-97/r14.anchor: قالوا ما نعبدهم، وحذف القول كثير

QURTUBI-FULL:21:96-97/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:96-97/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:96-97/r15.claim: Hiya refers to the eyes, and the following word abṣār explains it: when the promise comes, the eyes of disbelievers stare.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:96-97/r15.anchor: «هي» ضمير الأبصار، والأبصار المذكورة بعدها تفسير لها

QURTUBI-FULL:21:97/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:97/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:97/r1.claim: A poet's use of hiya before later naming the she-camel is cited as evidence for a pronoun whose referent appears afterward.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:97/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:97/r2.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:21:97/r2.claim: Al-Farra treats hiya as a supporting pronoun, as in the verse saying that it is not the eyes that go blind.

QURTUBI-FULL:21:97/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:97/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:97/r3.claim: Alternatively, the statement ends at hiya, meaning the Resurrection is present; the next clause front-loads its predicate, with the disbelievers' eyes staring from terror and scarcely blinking.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:97/r3.anchor: وقيل: إن الكلام تم عند قوله: «هي» التقدير: فإذا هي بمعنى القيامة

QURTUBI-FULL:21:97/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:21:97/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:21:97/r4.claim: The disbelievers cry woe because of the day's terror, admitting wrongdoing through disobedience and misplacing worship.
QURTUBI-FULL:21:97/r4.anchor: من هذا اليوم أي من هوله لا تكاد تطرف

BURSEVI:v5p399#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p399#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p399#3/r10.claim: The clause about the true promise is coordinated with the clause about the barrier opening.
BURSEVI:v5p399#3/r10.anchor: عطف على فتحت والمراد ما بعد النفخة الثانية

BURSEVI:v5p399#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p399#3/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p399#3/r11.claim: The true promise is what follows the second trumpet blast: resurrection, reckoning, and recompense.
BURSEVI:v5p399#3/r11.anchor: والمراد ما بعد النفخة الثانية من البعث والحساب والجزاء

BURSEVI:v5p399#3/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p399#3/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p399#3/r12.claim: The conditional answer uses sudden إذا; “she” is a pronoun of the event, and شاخصة is a fronted predicate of eyes.
BURSEVI:v5p399#3/r12.anchor: جواب الشرط وإذا للمفاجأة والضمير للقصة وشاخصة خبر مقدم لأبصار

BURSEVI:v5p399#3/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p399#3/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p399#3/r13.claim: Eyes are fixed open without blinking and raised in terror at the horror of Resurrection.
BURSEVI:v5p399#3/r13.anchor: يقال شخص بصره فهو شاخص إذا فتح عينيه وجعل لا يطرف

BURSEVI:v5p399#3/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p399#3/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p399#3/r14.claim: The Hour cannot be delayed after Yājūj and Mājūj emerge; Ḥudhayfa says a person could not ride a foal acquired then before it arrived.
BURSEVI:v5p399#3/r14.anchor: وفي الآية دلالة على أن قيام الساعة لا يتأخر عن خروج يأجوج ومأجوج كما روي عن حذيفة رضي الله عنه

BURSEVI:v5p400/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p400/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p400/r1.claim: Although the barrier opens near the world’s end and fixed gazes occur on Resurrection Day, the short interval between condition and result counts as no interval.
BURSEVI:v5p400/r1.anchor: فالجواب أن التفاوت القليل يجري مجرى العدم

BURSEVI:v5p400/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p400/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p400/r2.claim: The exclamation is supplied with an implied saying verb and cast as a circumstantial clause: they call woe to come since its time has arrived.
BURSEVI:v5p400/r2.anchor: وهو على تقدير قول وقع حالا من الموصول

BURSEVI:v5p400/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p400/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p400/r3.claim: They admit being wholly heedless in worldly life of resurrection and return to God for recompense.
BURSEVI:v5p400/r3.anchor: تامة في الدنيا والغفلة سهو يعتري من قلة التحفظ والتيقظ

BURSEVI:v5p400/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p400/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p400/r4.claim: Their correction rejects mere heedlessness: warned by signs, they were wrongdoers who denied them or exposed themselves to lasting punishment.
BURSEVI:v5p400/r4.anchor: إضراب عما قبله من وصف أنفسهم بالغفلة

BURSEVI:v5p400/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p400/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p400/r5.claim: A rational person should reflect on this reminder: God warned people and removed their excuses.
BURSEVI:v5p400/r5.anchor: فليتفكر العاقل في هذا البيان والتذكار فقد نبه الله وقطع الأعذار

BURSEVI:v5p400/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p400/r6.speaker: الله
BURSEVI:v5p400/r6.claim: God tells jinn and humans that He advised them, their deeds are recorded, and each person should praise Him for good or blame himself otherwise.
BURSEVI:v5p400/r6.anchor: يقول الله يا معشر الجن والإنس إني قد نصحت لكم

BURSEVI:v5p400/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p400/r7.speaker: بعض الحكماء
BURSEVI:v5p400/r7.claim: A sage says mourners should pity themselves instead: the dead has escaped seeing the Angel of Death, death agony, and fear of the final end.
BURSEVI:v5p400/r7.anchor: وعن بعض الحكماء أنه نظر إلى أناس يترحمون على ميت خلف جنازته

BURSEVI:v5p400/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p400/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p400/r8.claim: The author cites Saʿdī likening the body to a cage and the soul to a bird called breath, urging people to wake from heedlessness while opportunity remains.
BURSEVI:v5p400/r8.anchor: خبر دارى أي : استخواني قفس كه جان تو مرغيست نامش نفس

BURSEVI:v5p400/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p400/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p400/r9.claim: Saʿdī warns that time has passed in heedlessness and urges the listener to count a moment as an opportunity.
BURSEVI:v5p400/r9.anchor: جو مارا بغفلت بشد روزكار توبارى دمى ند فرصت شمار
